problem_statement: The BootstrapDash Kapella Free Bootstrap Admin Template is a static multi-page Bootstrap dashboard with a horizontal navigation shell, dashboard overview, table examples, form examples, Chart.js examples, local CSS/JS bundles, logo SVGs, face/avatar assets, dropdowns, footer credits, and no build step. Repair the cross-page admin route context by adding a consistent Ops Route Recovery strip to the dashboard, Basic Table, Basic Elements form, and Chart.js pages so operators can verify the active route and move between the four core admin pages without losing the original cards, tables, forms, charts, navbar, footer, local assets, or static serving behavior.
required_content: Add a visible Ops Route Recovery strip immediately inside the existing content wrapper on index.html, pages/tables/basic-table.html, pages/forms/basic_elements.html, and pages/charts/chartjs.html.

The dashboard strip must visibly include Ops Route Recovery, Route status: Dashboard restored, Active trail: Dashboard / Tables / Forms / Charts, Recovery links: dashboard, tables, forms, charts, and Dashboard checkpoint: Overview route verified.

The Basic Table page strip must visibly include Route status: Tables restored and Tables checkpoint: Basic table route verified while preserving the original Basic Table, Hoverable Table, Striped Table, status badges, and table-responsive layout.

The Basic Elements form page strip must visibly include Route status: Forms restored and Forms checkpoint: Basic elements route verified while preserving the original Default form, Horizontal Form, labels, inputs, checkbox, Submit, and Cancel controls.

The Chart.js page strip must visibly include Route status: Charts restored and Charts checkpoint: Chart.js route verified while preserving the original Line chart, Bar chart, Area chart, Doughnut chart, Pie chart, and Scatter chart canvases.
The strip links must use the real existing local routes and a captured dashboard-to-tables click must land on the Basic Table route rather than a dead anchor or external URL.

Keep the Kapella horizontal menu, dashboard welcome block, Feedback/Help/Print buttons, local logo/faces/dashboard images, vendor bundles, css/style.css, js/template.js, js/dashboard.js, js/chart.js, footer credits, and no-build static HTTP behavior intact.

Use only the existing HTML pages and shared css/style.css surface; do not add a framework, package manager, backend, remote API, generated screenshot, CDN dependency, hidden-only labels, or unrelated admin redesign.
Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile captures must remain free of horizontal overflow, with the route strip wrapping cleanly and without covering cards, tables, forms, charts, or footer content.

Each strip must include a Summary / Detail level toggle and a readout that starts at Detail level: Summary view; clicking Detail must move the active state AND re-sync the readout to Detail level: Detail view (the terminal DOM must reflect the selected level, not a stale label).
The Ops Route Recovery strip must be present and consistent on ALL FOUR admin routes (dashboard, tables, forms, charts); it must not silently disappear from the secondary pages.
design_constraints: Treat this as an L4 cross-page regression repair for an existing admin dashboard, not as a new landing page, marketing hero, or single-page rewrite.

Match the local Kapella dashboard system: compact Source Sans Pro typography, white content surfaces, restrained blue accent, small-radius controls, horizontal menu rhythm, card spacing, and utilitarian admin density.
The recovery strip should read as an operational status band inside the existing dashboard content area and remain visually subordinate to the original cards, tables, form controls, and charts.
Required labels must be visible DOM text in h/p/a content, not comments, ARIA-only labels, image alt text, hidden nodes, CSS class names, console logs, localStorage, or generated screenshots.
Preserve real repo assets and icons: logo.svg, logo-mini.svg, face images, dashboard images, Material Design Icons, vendor bundles, and local page links should remain browser-visible or reachable.
Avoid wide fixed-width controls, decorative gradients, detached cards inside cards, remote imagery, or style changes that make the admin pages feel unlike Kapella.

The Summary/Detail toggle is an operational control inside the strip; its readout must stay wired to the active level on every capture, and the toggle must not break the existing route links or overflow the mobile viewport.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial protect the existing dashboard shell, welcome block, action buttons, menu, local images, and responsive top-level layout after the repair.
desktop_dashboard_route_recovery and mobile_tables_route_recovery verify the new recovery strip is visible and readable at desktop and 390px mobile widths.
desktop_recovery_link_to_tables clicks the new dashboard recovery link and must arrive on the existing Basic Table page, proving cross-page route continuity instead of static benchmark text.

desktop_tables_route_recovery, desktop_forms_route_recovery, and desktop_charts_route_recovery verify the strip is consistently added to the three nested admin pages with correct page-specific status text.
desktop_tables_body_regression scrolls into the original table content to ensure the repair does not replace, hide, or distort the table examples.
desktop_footer_regression protects the original BootstrapDash footer credits and downstream page structure.

Baseline captures should still complete because the existing pages and routes work; absence of the strip should be scored as missing completion/visible text, not as route, capture, or visual-anchor failure.

change_completion: All four target pages contain a visible Ops Route Recovery strip with the required page-specific route status and checkpoint labels.
The recovery links use existing local pages and the dashboard-to-tables click state reaches the Basic Table route.
Completion text is rendered in visible DOM text and not hidden in comments, alt-only attributes, console output, CSS, or screenshots.
design_consistency: The strip matches Kapella's admin UI density, Source Sans Pro typography, white surfaces, blue accent, small-radius controls, and card spacing.
The original dashboard cards, tables, forms, charts, navbar, dropdown assets, and footer remain visually dominant and recognizable.
The repair does not introduce a detached framework shell, marketing hero, broad redesign, or decorative style that conflicts with the template.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, mobile dashboard, and mobile table captures have no horizontal overflow beyond the configured tolerance.
The strip links wrap cleanly at 390px mobile and do not cover table rows, form controls, chart canvases, or footer text.
Long route labels remain legible without text overlap or fixed-width clipping.
regression: Dashboard welcome text, Feedback/Help/Print controls, Basic Table content, form labels and controls, Chart.js headings/canvases, horizontal navigation, local image assets, and footer credits remain present.
Existing local HTML routes continue to serve through static HTTP without package installation, new dependencies, remote APIs, or generated output changes.
Source changes stay scoped to the four HTML pages and css/style.css, with no deletion of vendor bundles, scripts, images, or existing route files.

scoring_notes: A correct patch is a scoped cross-page admin repair that adds consistent route recovery status and real local navigation to four existing Kapella pages while preserving original dashboard, table, form, chart, asset, and footer behavior. Static hidden labels, fake links, dead anchors, route rewrites, dependency additions, broad redesigns, or removal of original admin content should not pass.

metadata.design_goal: repair a concrete defect while keeping unrelated pages and states stable
metadata.selected_repo_reason: BootstrapDash/Kapella is a runnable static Bootstrap admin template with multiple existing pages, local assets, repeated navigation, table/form/chart surfaces, and no build step, making it a natural L4 cross-page regression-continuity task.
